purpose: Resolve legal terms according to the applicable Irish legal regime, temporal version and provision rather than ordinary-language assumptions.
core_principle: TERM → REGIME → DEFINING SOURCE → VERSION → SCOPE → LEGAL MEANING
rules: Ordinary dictionary meaning is not a substitute for a statutory definition where one applies.
The same word may have different legal meanings in different statutes or regimes.
A definition may be limited to a particular Part, section, scheme or procedural context.
Current definitions cannot automatically be projected backward to historical events.
An amendment to a definition requires commencement and transitional analysis.
Case law may clarify an undefined or disputed term but cannot be treated as a statutory definition unless the source supports that proposition.
Official guidance may explain operational use but does not override the defining legislation.
priority_rules: Exact governing provision and regime first.
Specific statutory definition before general usage where applicable.
Applicable temporal version before current consolidated wording.
Relevant special regime before broad general property terminology.
Case law only within its actual interpretive scope.
Unresolved material definition means legal analysis remains incomplete.
hard_stops: Never select a definition solely from word similarity.
Never merge definitions from different statutes without authority.
Never treat ordinary-language ownership as registered title.
Never use a current definition for a historical question without temporal verification.
Never hide a material unresolved definition.
